title: Terminal/chat: list every coding agent on this computer; plain error for an older engine; readable Grok steps
body:
Owner, 2026-10-01, OpenAgents Terminal on the Mac (screenshots in the session):

1. **The welcome card says only "Coder  Codex ready"** though this Mac has Codex, Claude Code, Grok Build, and Devin. Cause: `Here::context` (`crates/coder/src/task/chat_client.rs`) builds the engines from `Local::predict` → `Engine::from_runner`: the engine that would run plus those passed over before it. Engines later in the order are never probed, and an opt-in engine (Devin, OpenCode) not in `coder.providers` is skipped as NotAllowed. Fix: list every coding agent installed or signed in on this computer with its own state: ready, not signed in, at its usage limit, or **not enabled** (installed but not in `coder.providers`), in the settings' order. Use the same per-provider login and capacity reads the host's engine report uses (#10018, #10105), and never read a token. The same list goes to the chat worker's `context.computer.engines`: raise `MAX_ENGINES` (4) to cover all five agents where the wire allows, and update the NIP/INVARIANTS bound. Do the same on the desktop's welcome or sidebar if it shares the code.
2. **"Coder could not start: the controller refused the launch: {\"error\":\"the execution grant has an invalid shape\"}"** came from a dev `openagents` using an older `~/.openagents/bin/microcoder` (07:36 today, before #10103 dropped `max_steps`), which can't read the newer grant. (The owner's `terminal` shell function now builds `microcoder` beside the binary.) Product fix: never show raw JSON. When the engine refuses a grant's shape, say in one plain sentence that the Coder engine at PATH is older than this program and how to update it (reinstall the app, or rebuild). Consider a grant/engine version handshake (`microcoder --grant-version` or similar) checked before launch, so the start says so before starting.
3. **Grok Build steps render as raw tool JSON** in the transcript (`other {\"target_directory\":…}`, `other {\"target_file\":…/README.md}`). Map Grok's ACP tool kinds to the same readable step lines as the other engines ("Read README.md", "Listed scratch-…"), with a short fallback for unknown kinds, never raw JSON.

Tests for each. Then a terminal pty scenario showing all engines on the welcome card from a stand-in home where several agents are signed in.
